scope: Opt-in monitoring email notifications using the existing Gmail send-only mailbox and hourly dispatcher
implemented: Verified application account recipient only, including explicitly linked preview workspaces; no client-chosen recipient
Completed, partial and failed monitored reports; quota/configuration launch failures without a report notify once per due occurrence
Durable D1 outbox with unique report/event identity, concurrent claims, explicit rejection retries and saved Gmail receipts
Opt-out suppresses pending mail; changed verification/recipient suppresses queued mail; no historical backfill on opt-in
Test email with 30-minute per-owner limit; sender authorization check and latest 20 private delivery statuses
OAuth Testing expiry warning; authorization errors block and resume after operator reconnect
Interrupted/ambiguous sends and lost receipts require explicit duplicate-risk acknowledgement before manual retry
Shared transport for verification/reset emails with bounded safe pre-send retries and redacted health telemetry

validation.realGmail: One test email accepted by Gmail from an isolated Worker/D1 using existing sender credentials; no production data or research usage changed
validation.inboxReceipt: Operator confirmed the real test message arrived in the inbox on 17 October 2026; no inbox-read scope was used
validation.browser: Interactive browser tool is unavailable in this turn; no claim of live authenticated UI walkthrough

limits: Google OAuth remains Testing by explicit operator request; Gmail refresh consent can expire after seven days. This release cannot provide indefinite unattended delivery.
Gmail receipt means accepted by Gmail, not a deliverability guarantee or inbox receipt.
Hourly dispatch and backlog can delay mail; individual messages retry at most eight send attempts and expire after seven days. Blocked authorization checks do not consume send attempts.
No report body, source contents, uploads, public-share tokens or verification/reset links in monitoring emails.
No new sender account/provider, paid service, timezone change, theme change or customer-wide automatic opt-in.
rollback: Revert Worker source to v21 while retaining the three additive tables. No old tables or auth settings are changed; disable notification settings before rollback if needed.
